**Setup.** Label the root $A$, the left child $B$ (value 2), the right child $C$ (value 6), and the leaves $D$ (value 1), $E$ (value 3), $F$ (value 5), $G$ (value 7). Then $p(a)=P(\text{token } a \text{ reaches } A \text{ before token } 7)$. Each token moves along a chosen edge only if that edge touches its position. When both tokens sit on the same edge, they swap. So the two tokens are not independent, and the joint chain on pairs of positions must be used.

Let $g(x,y)$ be the probability that the token at $x$ reaches $A$ before the token at $y$. Then $g(A,y)=1$, $g(x,A)=0$, and $g(x,y)+g(y,x)=1$. The rule for a state $(x,y)$ is
$$(\deg x+\deg y-\mathbf{1}_{x\sim y})\,g(x,y)=\sum_{\text{edges touching }x\text{ or }y} v_e,$$
where $v_e$ is the value of the resulting state (or the boundary value if a token reaches $A$).

**Symmetry.** The tree automorphisms give $g(B,C)=\tfrac12$, $g(D,E)=g(F,G)=\tfrac12$, $g(D,F)=g(D,G)=g(E,F)=g(E,G)=\tfrac12$, $g(B,D)=g(B,E)=g(C,F)=g(C,G)=p$, and $g(B,F)=g(B,G)=g(C,D)=g(C,E)=q$.

- $(D,E)$: $2g=g(B,E)+g(D,B)=p+(1-p)=1$, so $g(D,E)=\tfrac12$.
- $(D,F)$: $2g=g(B,F)+g(D,C)=q+(1-q)=1$, so $g(D,F)=\tfrac12$.
- $(B,D)$: $3p=1+g(E,D)+g(D,B)=1+\tfrac12+(1-p)$, so $p=\tfrac58$.
- $(B,F)$: $4q=1+g(D,F)+g(E,F)+g(B,C)=1+\tfrac12+\tfrac12+\tfrac12$, so $q=\tfrac58$.
- $(B,C)$: $6m=3$, so $m=\tfrac12$, which is consistent with the symmetry.

I also checked the remaining state types directly, such as $(C,G)$, $(F,G)$, $(D,C)$, $(B,G)$, $(C,F)$, and $(E,F)$. They all agree with these values.

**Answer.** The initial positions are $1$ at $D$, $2$ at $B$, $3$ at $E$, $5$ at $F$, and $6$ at $C$, while $7$ starts at $G$. So
$$p(1)+p(2)+p(3)+p(5)+p(6)=g(D,G)+g(B,G)+g(E,G)+g(F,G)+g(C,G)=\tfrac12+\tfrac58+\tfrac12+\tfrac12+\tfrac58=\tfrac{11}{4}.$$
